notes: v2.5.19 - required update. A purchase order line that buys a kit can now be received as its separate parts, purchasing, receiving and inventory all describe a kit the same way, receiving can override a refusal to split one, and a job is charged for the whole kit it opened rather than the half it used. A requisition line that has already been received is never handed back as outstanding; cancelling a purchase order or deleting one of its lines releases the requisition lines behind it; reopening a cancelled order puts it back in front of an approver; and one order can no longer carry the same requisition line twice. Every unit dropdown in the application now offers the same list - requisition line units are spelled the way purchasing codes are spelled, so about 190 existing lines read differently without having changed, older spellings are recognised instead of quietly falling back, and pails, drums and the other container sizes are selectable at last. A new Materials screen under Catalog lets you add, rename, recategorise or retire a material; a rename now moves everywhere the name is used in one action; and being told a material is already taken names the part holding it and points at the field that resolves it, before you save rather than after. Receiving goods now actually ticks Assembly Ready, a recorded vendor receipt counts as on hand in its own right, and Assembly Readiness counts pieces on both sides of the slash - so some readiness figures will rise on their own, and periods spanning this update are not comparable with periods before it. Editing a part location no longer silently un-kits it, a bulk edit tells every open page what else it changed, and a batch sign-off records the drawing revision it was signed off at. On the shop terminals a location is remembered per badge holder rather than per terminal, a scan no longer un-kits the part it has just kitted, and scan history records what a scan did rather than who ran it, which roughly doubles the Receiving scans figure on Debriefing without rewriting history. Planner assignments can be removed without opening the picker and milestones with a department are no longer hidden outside the gantt. A project manager can publish an approved router to the floor, a step going In Progress no longer clocks on the entire roster, and figures we cannot stand behind read as absent instead of as fact. Risk Management can be recorded as the source of a nonconformance, cancelling one asks why and shows the reason, and the CAPA edit screen no longer opens blank. CATIA streaming forwards your mouse and keyboard reliably, drops far fewer sessions for no reason, and allows only one session per machine. The wiki no longer blocks legitimate pages, and the client purchase order build filter can include records that belong to the project rather than to one build. This release also updates the database behind AOS, so please update as soon as you are prompted.
